items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: Dorian Hall, this singer, who is a black cat on James’s band and I were in the museum together

ctx.x: Is there something about the times and the state of society that you think might make what you’re describing very hard to ever reproduce? And the reason I ask that is I spoke to Rashied Ali once and was trying to get at the attitude of the musicians when he played in late Coltrane’s life. And he just kept saying, “Listen, the times were different. The bebop people had their time, this was our time.” So I’m not asking this question very well but do you think that the time and space that John Coltrane was doing…

Well I’m sure it did and especially, you know I think about this because I was very lucky to get to play a lot with Bob Cranshaw for instance and with Frank Wess and with Joe, and those musicians, Clark Terry, those guys, they treated everybody with such dignity and respect. And you know that they weren’t treated with dignity and respect, but they were so elegant and so — they were big people, big humans. A couple of days ago we were in Jackson, Mississippi and Dorian Hall, this singer, who is a black cat on…
going to change. Like sometimes I think the original sin is so great that you know what I mean? I’m an optimistic person but there are times when it’s like wow.
